newsitem.title: QATAR: Qatar shares continue upswing in robust trade.
newsitem.headline: Qatar shares continue upswing in robust trade.

text.p: Shares on Qatar's new stock market continued their upward swing, with robust trade pushing the index up 1.4 percent to a new record high in the week to Thursday, brokers said.
"The volume of trade at the official Doha Securities Market (DSM) rose 120 percent to 30,891 shares compared to 13,953 in the previous week," DSM information officer Jamal Rihawi said.

But the value of trade dropped 21 percent to 4.92 million riyals from 6.21 million a week earlier. The total number of deals rose to 25 from 20. Seven shares advanced, two lost ground and eight were unchanged.

The Commercial Bank of Qatar's 17-share index rose 1.91 points to 135.82 points from 133.91 in the previous week. The exchange, which launched formal operations on May 27, has not yet set up its own official index.

The banking sector took the lead in the week with 29,991 shares valued at 3.68 million riyals changing hands. It was followed by the services sector with 2,994 shares valued at 180,859 riyals, industrials with 2,030 shares at 190,950 riyals and insurance with 1,876 shares at 870,437 riyals, Rihawi said.

Qatar National Bank, which accounts for a third of the total market capitalisation of around $1.9 billion, led the upswing with a solid 17 riyal jump in its share price to 580. Qatar Navigation rose 10 riyals to 750 and Qatar International Islamic Bank gained nine riyals to 103.50.
Qatar Insurance declined nine riyals to 560 and Qatar Cement shed five riyals to 300.
